sources.title: Tokenization Attacks on LLMs - hiddenlayer.com
sources.snippet: Learn how attackers exploit tokenization in Large Language Models (LLMs) through glitch tokens, invisible Unicode attacks, and TokenBreak techniques to bypass AI security safeguards and manipulate model behavior.

sources.title: Tokenizer Tampering - docs.hiddenlayer.ai
sources.snippet: The model's tokenizer.json contains two or more tokens that share the same token ID. Tokenizers assume each ID maps to a single token. An attacker can add a malicious token with the same ID as an existing one, giving them control over what text the model outputs for that ID. sources.title: Ox Alpha: What We Know So Far (Aug 2026) | explainx.ai Blog
sources.snippet: Ox Alpha (aka "0x Alpha"): what we actually know. Fingerprinting matched its tokenizer and video encoder to GLM-5.3, ruling out MiMo, Qwen, GLM-4.6V.

sources.title: Tokenizer Tampering - hiddenlayer.com
sources.snippet: HiddenLayer researchers demonstrate how tokenizer tampering can enable silent AI supply chain attacks, including command substitution, tool-call injection, and data exfiltration.
